name: Visual Question Answering Datasets Survey
description: A review paper critically examining the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA) in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets (DAQUAR, COCO-QA, The VQA Dataset, FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome, SHAPES), evaluation metrics, and algorithms. The paper discusses limitations of current datasets with regard to their ability to properly train and assess VQA algorithms, exhaustively reviews existing algorithms, and discusses possible future directions for VQA and image understanding research.
creator: Kushal Kafle, Christopher Kanan
citeAs: Kafle, K. and Kanan, C. (2017). Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv:1610.01465v4 [cs.CV].
rai:dataCollection: Multiple VQA datasets were collected using different methods: DAQUAR used images from NYU-DepthV2 with manual and automated QA pair generation; COCO-QA used an NLP algorithm to derive QA pairs from COCO image captions; The VQA Dataset (COCO-VQA) used Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate questions and answers; FM-IQA collected human-generated questions and answers originally in Chinese with English translations; Visual Genome used crowdsourced dense image annotations with both free-form and region-specific question prompting; Visual7W is a subset of Visual Genome; SHAPES consists of programmatically generated questions about synthetic shape images.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, User-generated content data, Software Collection, Others
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The authors were unable to retrieve the English version of the FM-IQA dataset from the provided download link.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from: NYU-DepthV2 Dataset (DAQUAR), Microsoft COCO dataset with 328,000 images (COCO-QA, COCO-VQA, FM-IQA, Visual7W), COCO and YFCC100M/Flickr100M (Visual Genome), and synthetic cartoon images (SYNTH-VQA, SHAPES). QA pairs were generated via NLP algorithms, crowdsourcing (Amazon Mechanical Turk), and manual annotation.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Datasets released beginning in 2014; the review covers datasets available as of the article's writing (up to June 2017).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For COCO-VQA multiple-choice format, 18 answer choices were constructed comprising: the correct answer (most frequent answer from 10 annotators), 3 plausible answers (collected from annotators without seeing the image), top 10 most popular answers in the dataset, and randomly selected correct answers for other questions. For Visual7W pointing questions, four plausible bounding boxes were provided as multiple-choice options.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: COCO-QA QA pairs were generated by an NLP algorithm that derives questions from COCO image captions; longer sentences were broken into smaller chunks for processing. DAQUAR-37 is a reduced configuration with only 37 object categories. DAQUAR-consensus collected additional ground truth answers for an alternative evaluation metric. Visual Genome used both free-form and region-specific question prompting to reduce bias in question types.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For COCO-VQA: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were asked to 'Stump a smart robot' to generate questions, and a separate pool of workers generated answers; each question was answered by 10 independent annotators. For DAQUAR-consensus: an average of five human-annotated ground truth answers per question were collected. For Visual Genome: annotators used both free-form and region-specific prompting methods to generate QA pairs. For SYNTH-VQA: 3 questions per scene with 10 ground truth answers per question. FM-IQA used human judges to assess answer quality on a 3-point scale (0=totally wrong, 1=partially correct, 2=perfectly correct).
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for COCO-VQA annotation.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is approximately 83.3% using the AccuracyVQA metric. Over 59% of 'Why' questions have fewer than three annotators giving exactly the same answer. More than 13% of yes/no answers have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators. Simple questions can evoke diverse answers; annotators sometimes provide antonymous answers (e.g., left and right). The AccuracyVQA metric awards full score if the algorithm agrees with 3 or more out of 10 annotators.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper notes that as of the article's writing, no methods had been evaluated on Visual Genome beyond the baselines established by the authors. No explicit versioning or deprecation policies are described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: SYNTH-VQA human cartoon models span different age, gender, and races to provide variation in appearance.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA has potential applications as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals, enabling them to get information about images on the web and in the real world. It could also improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content, and be used for image retrieval without using image meta-data or tags.
rai:dataBiases: Language biases are a major issue: question-only models achieve up to 49.6% accuracy on COCO-VQA without using images. In COCO-VQA, 'yes/no' answers span about 38% of all questions and 59% are answered 'yes'. Answering 'yes' to all yes/no questions yields 71% accuracy instead of the expected ~50%. Questions about color, objects, and scenes have strong language priors. VQA systems are sensitive to question phrasing. Natural image datasets have contextual biases (e.g., street scenes more likely to have dogs than zebras). COCO-QA is limited to four question types derived from captions. DAQUAR contains exclusively indoor scenes.
rai:dataLimitations: DAQUAR is too small to train complex models and contains only indoor scenes with clutter and extreme lighting; human accuracy is only 50.2%. COCO-QA has grammatical errors and nonsensical questions due to flaws in the NLP generation algorithm, and only four question types. COCO-VQA contains subjective and opinion-seeking questions without single objective answers, and has strong language biases. FM-IQA requires human judges for evaluation, making it impractical for iterative development. Visual Genome's long-tailed answer distribution makes open-ended evaluation challenging. Current datasets are not large enough (performance has not plateaued as a function of training data size). All datasets use evaluation metrics that treat every question with equal weight, disadvantaging rare question types.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of VQA algorithms. Benchmarking visual question answering systems. Evaluating image understanding capabilities. The datasets support both open-ended and multiple-choice evaluation paradigms. Recommended future use includes per-question-type evaluation rather than overall accuracy to better assess algorithm capabilities.
rai:annotationsPerItem: COCO-VQA: 3 questions per image, 10 answers per question. SYNTH-VQA: 3 questions per scene, 10 ground truth answers per question. DAQUAR-consensus: average of 5 human-annotated ground truth answers per question. Visual Genome: average of 17 QA pairs per image.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLP algorithm used to generate QA pairs from COCO captions for COCO-QA. Word2vec used for computing similarity between question words and object labels in the FDA model. Edge Boxes used for generating bounding box region proposals. ResNet, VGGNet, and GoogLeNet CNNs used for image feature extraction in various algorithms.
